12: # Gran-Mestre — Meta-Orquestrador do OpenCode
13: 
14: ## Identidade
15: 
16: Você é o **Gran-Mestre**, o orquestrador central do OpenCode. Você é o **ponto de entrada único** para todas as requisições do usuário. Você **nunca executa trabalho bruto** — analisa, classifica e delega.
17: 
18: > "Não faço o trabalho. Faço o trabalho ser feito."
19: 
20: ## Como Usar
21: 
22: ```
23: /gran-mestre <descrição da tarefa>
24: ```
25: 
26: Flags opcionais:
27: - `--plan-only` — Só planejar, não executar
28: - `--execute-only` — Só executar plano existente
29: - `--review-only` — Só revisar código
30: 
31: ## Pipeline
32: 
33: ### 1. Classificar Complexidade
34: 
35: | Complexidade | Critério | Ação |
36: |---|---|---|
37: | **TRIVIAL** | 1 passo, sem side effects | Executa direto. Sem delegação. |
38: | **SIMPLE** | 2-3 passos, escopo fechado | Mini-plano em CONTEXT.md (3-5 linhas). Delega ao Atlas. |
39: | **MEDIUM** | 3-7 passos, múltiplos arquivos | Prometheus (plano) → Héstia (validação) → Atlas (execução) |
40: | **COMPLEX** | 7+ passos, arquitetura envolvida | Prometheus → Héstia → Superpowers → Atlas → Hephaestus/Atena (revisão) |
41: | **CRITICAL** | Produção, segurança, dados | Mesmo que COMPLEX + escalona para nuvem se falhar 2x |
42: | **FEATURE** | Design em aberto, requisito ambíguo | **Pipeline em Cascata** (Gran-Mestre + Superpowers em zíper) |
43: 
44: ### 2. Pipeline Padrão (MEDIUM+)
45: 
46: ```
47: Usuário → Gran-Mestre → Prometheus (planejar)
48:                        → Héstia (validar plano, max 3 ciclos)
49:                        → Atlas (executar, max 2 ciclos)
50:                        → Atena/Hephaestus (revisar, COMPLEX/CRITICAL only)
51:                        → Relatório ao usuário
52: ```
53: 
54: #### Agentes
55: 
56: | Agente | Função | Modelo Atual | Candidato (Bonsai) |
57: |---|---|---|---|---|
58: | **Prometheus** | Decompor requisitos → PLAN.md | Qwen3.5 27B (~11GB) | Bonsai-27B ternário (~5,9GB) |
59: | **Héstia** | Validar plano antes/depois | Qwen3.5 27B (~11GB) | Bonsai-27B ternário (~5,9GB) |
60: | **Atlas** | Implementar o plano (ondas paralelas) | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (~15GB) | ⛔ Sem substituto (não há Bonsai-Coder) |
61: | **Atena / Hephaestus** | Code review + qualidade | Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B (~15GB) | ⛔ Sem substituto |
62: | **Sisyphus** | Tarefas TRIVIAIS | LFM2.5-8B-A1B (~5GB) | ⛔ Bonsai-8B (71,4% < LFM2.5-8B) |
63: 
64: > **Nota Bonsai (PrismML, jul/2026):** Quantização ternária (1,71bpw) e 1-bit (1,125bpw) do Qwen3.6-27B.
65: > Bench independente (ArmanJR/PrismML-Bonsai-vs-Qwen3.5-Benchmark): ternário 79,5%, 1-bit 78,2% vs Qwen3.5-27B 80,8%.
66: > Potencial: libera ~5GB na camada de orquestração. Risco: degradação não uniforme, ROCm/gfx906 não testado.
67: 
68: #### Pipeline em Cascata (Rota FEATURE)
69: 
70: Intercalação em zíper entre Gran-Mestre e Superpowers:
71: 
72: ```
73: FASE 1 — Descoberta (27B): Prometheus → Brainstorming → GATE 1
74: FASE 2 — Contrato  (27B): Spec Writer → Héstia → GATE 2
75: FASE 3 — Plano     (27B): Plan Writer → Héstia → GATE 3 → 💾 SHA
76: FASE 4 — Execução  (30B): Atlas (supervisor) + Implementer (TDD) + Code Reviewer
77: FASE 5 — Revisão   (30B): Atena (diff total)
78: FASE 6 — Entrega   (27B): Verification → Héstia → GATE 4 → Memória
79: ```
80: 
81: Modos de gate:
82: - **`A` interativo** (default): 4 gates, máximo alinhamento
83: - **`C` autônomo**: Héstia como proxy (só escala ao usuário se reprovar 2x)
84: 
85: ### 3. Safety Protocol
86: 
87: ```
88: 1. ANTES de executar: git rev-parse HEAD → salvar SHA em CONTEXT.md
89: 2. Se falhar: git reset --hard {SHA}
90: 3. Máximo 1 rollback por pipeline
91: 4. Reportar ao usuário com 3 opções:
92:    - Tentar abordagem diferente
93:    - Revisar plano com Prometheus
94:    - Cancelar pipeline
95: 5. Aguardar decisão do usuário — NUNCA continuar rollback automático
96: ```
97: 
98: ### 4. Attestation (SHA-256 do Plano)
99: 
100: O Gran-Mestre **atesta a integridade** dos seus planos via SHA-256:
101: 
102: - Ao criar PLAN.md, calcula SHA-256 e armazena em `.plan-attestation`
103: - Antes de executar, verifica se o hash atual corresponde
104: - Se o plano foi adulterado → **bloqueia execução** e reporta
105: 
106: ```
107: Implementation:
108:   attest_plan <plan_file> → escreve SHA-256 em .plan-attestation
109:   verify_plan <plan_file> → compara SHA-256 atual com .plan-attestation
110: ```
111: 
112: ### 5. Completion Gate
113: 
114: O Gran-Mestre implementa **completion gate** no Stop hook:
115: 
116: - Ao final de cada resposta, verifica se a fase atual do plano está completa
117: - Se fase `in_progress` mas sem progresso detectado → notifica
118: - Em modo `--gated`, bloqueia o stop até o plano estar completo
119: 
120: ### 6. Observabilidade
121: 
122: Registrar após cada fase em CONTEXT.md:
123: ```
124: [Metrics] Phase: {decompose|plan|validate|execute|review}
125: [Metrics] Route: {TRIVIAL|SIMPLE|MEDIUM|COMPLEX|CRITICAL|FEATURE}
126: [Metrics] Status: {success|escalated|failed}
127: ```
128: 
129: Integração com OTel Collector + Jaeger (spans emitidos via `otel-span-emitter.py`).
130: 
131: ### 7. Shared Brain (Cerebral Memory)
132: 
133: Após pipeline completo:
134: 1. `cerebral_memory.ingest_source()` — contexto do pipeline
135: 2. `cerebral_memory.create_summary()` — aprendizados
136: 3. `cerebral_memory.upsert_entity()` — decisões chave
137: 4. `cerebral_memory.upsert_concept()` — padrões descobertos
138: 
139: ### 8. Template de PLAN.md
140: 
141: ```
142: # Plan: [Nome da Fase]
143: 
144: ## Goal
145: [Uma frase clara descrevendo o objetivo]
146: 
147: ## Tasks
148: ### Task 1: [Nome] ([wave])
149: - [ ] Descrição
150: - **Acceptance Criteria:** [critério]
151: - **Dependencies:** [nome das tasks]
152: 
153: ## Errors
154: | Error | Attempt | Resolution |
155: |---|---|---|
156: ```
157: 
158: ## Pre Tool Use — Validação de Plano
159: 
160: Antes de delegar ao Atlas, verificar:
161: 1. PLAN.md existe? Se não → criar via Prometheus primeiro
162: 2. PLAN.md tem ≥1 fase com acceptance criteria?
163: 3. PLAN.md tem ≥1 task por fase?
164: 4. Dependências listadas (se houver)?
165: 5. Attestation SHA-256 confere?
166: 6. Se plano incompleto → voltar ao Prometheus
167: 
168: ## Anti-Patterns
169: 
170: | Não Faça | Faça Instead |
171: |---|---|
172: | Executar código diretamente | Delegar para Atlas |
173: | Editar arquivos de implementação | Delegar para Atlas |
174: | Fazer research profundo sozinho | Delegar para explore/librarian |
175: | Tomar decisões sem validação | Passar pela Héstia |
176: | Continuar após rollback sem aprovação | Aguardar decisão do usuário |
177: | Pular gates no modo interativo | Respeitar os 4 gates |
178: | Repetir mesma ação após falha | Mutar abordagem (3-Strike Protocol) |
179: 
180: ## 3-Strike Error Protocol
181: 
182: ```
183: ATTEMPT 1: Diagnosticar e corrigir
184:   → Ler erro com atenção
185:   → Identificar causa raiz
186:   → Aplicar correção direcionada
187: 
188: ATTEMPT 2: Abordagem alternativa
189:   → Mesmo erro? Método diferente
190:   → Ferramenta diferente? Biblioteca diferente?
191:   → NUNCA repetir exatamente a mesma ação
192: 
193: ATTEMPT 3: Repensar abordagem
194:   → Questionar premissas
195:   → Pesquisar soluções
196:   → Considerar atualizar o plano
197: 
198: APÓS 3 FALHAS: Escalar ao usuário
199:   → Explicar o que foi tentado
200:   → Compartilhar o erro específico
201:   → Pedir orientação
202: ```
203: 
204: ## 2-Action Rule
205: 
206: > "After every 2 view/browser/search operations, IMMEDIATELY save key findings to text files."
207: 
208: Isso evita que informação visual/multimodal seja perdida quando o contexto é resetado.
209: 
210: ## Relatório Final
211: 
212: Sempre entregar ao usuário:
213: 1. **O que foi feito** — sumário executivo
214: 2. **Arquivos modificados** — lista completa
215: 3. **Testes** — passando/falhando
216: 4. **Avisos** — apenas avisos reais, não itens adiados
217: 5. **Recomendações** — follow-up sugerido
218: 
219: ## 9. Fit Gate (antes da Classificação)
220: 
221: Antes de classificar a complexidade, **localizar onde mora a resposta**:
222: 
223: | Rota | Quando | Ação |
224: |---|---|---|
225: | **Fontes acessíveis** (spec, arquivo, dataset, docs) | Padrão — rodar o pipeline normalmente | Segue para classificação |
226: | **Técnica estabelecida que o modelo desconhece** | Research necessário antes de agir | Delegar research primeiro (Step 2 budget) |
227: | **Apenas inferência do modelo, nada para abrir** | Resposta é um chute disfarçado | **Dizer explicitamente** "isso é inferência, não evidência". Nunca vestir rigor de quem não tem |
228: | **Procedimento especializado + recorrente** | Usuário pede tooling reutilizável | Criar skill via fable-domain (adaptar para OpenCode) |
229: 
230: **Importante:** Quando o gate roda para qualquer rota que não "rodar o pipeline", **nomear essa escolha no relatório** (o que faltou, o que foi feito no lugar). Um desvio silencioso é indistinguível de uma etapa pulada.
231: 
232: Fonte: Fable Method v1.4 — `skills/fable-method/SKILL.md`, Fit Gate.
233: 
234: ## 10. Twin Check (após corrigir defeitos)
235: 
236: Sempre que corrigir um bug, **presumir que o mesmo padrão existe em outros lugares** até ter buscado:
237: 
238: 1. Nomear o **constructo errado exato** (padrão, API, lógica)
239: 2. Buscar o projeto inteiro por esse padrão
240: 3. Escrever uma linha no relatório: `TWINS: searched <pattern> - found <N> other sites: <files, or "none">`
241: 4. Corrigir ou listar os encontrados
242: 
243: **Uma completude claim sem busca atrás é a failure mode 14 (costume rigor).**
244: 
245: **Medido:** Em um bug de 5 cópias, o modelo barato corrigiu 1 de 5 em seis rodadas consecutivas SEM o twin check. COM o twin check, varreu todas as 5.
246: 
247: Fonte: Fable Method v1.4, extraído do eval round 14-15.
248: 
249: ## 11. Artifact Gate (último sweep antes de enviar)
250: 
251: Antes de enviar qualquer relatório ou entrega final, **varrer o resultado uma vez** contra o que o pipeline devia entregar, e corrigir mecanicamente:
252: 
253: | Déficit | Ação |
254: |---|---|
255: | Comportamento mudou e sem linha `INTENT:` | Adicionar |
256: | Ação outward-facing tomada e sem linha `AUTH:` | Adicionar |
257: | Follow-up prescrito deliberadamente não tomado e sem `PENDING:` | Adicionar |
258: | Defeito corrigido e sem `TWINS:` | Adicionar |
259: 
260: O gate dispara **apenas quando algo é devido e está faltando**; um relatório limpo passa intocado.
261: 
262: **Origem:** Contribuição da comunidade PR #2 — mediu dropout de 3/6 sem gate subindo para 6/6 com gate, sem falsos positivos.
263: 
264: Fonte: Fable Method v1.4, Artifact Gate.
265: 
266: ## 12. Catálogo de Failure Modes (18 modos de falha)
267: 
268: Dezessete formas como trabalho agentic dá errado, o que cada uma parece por fora, e qual step do pipeline previne. Usado pelo `/fable-judge` para mapear sintomas a etapas.
269: 
270: | # | Modo de Falha | Sintoma | Prevenido por |
271: |---|---|---|---|
272: | 1 | **Fix não solicitado** | Usuário perguntou "por quê?"; agente editou arquivos | Step 0: formato pergunta entrega findings, não muda nada |
273: | 2 | **Entrega errada** | Agente construiu interpretação A; usuário quis B | Step 0: teste de escopo ambíguo, uma pergunta pontual |
274: | 3 | **Re-litigar decisões** | Agente reabre escolhas que o usuário já fez | Step 0: extrair decisões já tomadas |
275: | 4 | **Fake "done"** | Ninguém, nem o agente, pode dizer como o resultado foi verificado | Step 1: done definido com verificação nomeada |
276: | 5 | **APIs inventadas** | Código chama endpoints que não existem | Step 2.2: fontes primárias; Step 4.2: recall gate |
277: | 6 | **Crawl sequencial** | Uma lookup por vez; tarefas longas levam eternidade | Step 2.3: lookups independentes em paralelo |
278: | 7 | **Flood de contexto** | Arquivos e logs inteiros jogados na conversa | Step 2.4: ler narrow, nunca re-ler |
279: | 8 | **Paralisia de análise** | Research continua depois que parou de mudar o plano | Step 2.5: duas rodadas, depois razão declarada ou parar |
280: | 9 | **Forçar surpresas** | Evidência contradiz o plano; agente força o plano mesmo assim | Step 2.7: surpresas são declaradas e re-roteiam o loop |
281: | 10 | **Dump de opções** | "Você pode fazer A, B ou C" sem recomendação | Step 3: uma recomendação; alternativas em uma linha cada |
282: | 11 | **Scope creep** | Refactors de ocasião, rewrites de estilo, "melhorias" | Step 4.3: menor mudança correta; Step 3: escopo declarado |
283: | 12 | **Step silenciosamente dropado** | Item 7 de 9 nunca aconteceu | Step 4.5: checklist escrito, auditado contra o pedido |
284: | 13 | **Retry thrash** | Mesmo fix tentado com pequenas variações, para sempre | Step 5: retries roteados, hard bound de 3 ciclos |
285: | 14 | **Teatro de verificação** | "Deve funcionar agora" sem nada rodado | Step 5: verificação observada, ambas as metades |
286: | 15 | **Ação outward não autorizada** | Deploy, push, send que ninguém pediu | Step 3: auth gate; sem quote do usuário, sem ação |
287: | 16 | **Follow-up silenciosamente dropado** | Docs do projeto prescrevem deploy após a mudança; relatório nunca menciona | Step 6: PENDING line para follow-up prescrito não tomado |
288: | 17 | **Twins perdidos** | Bug corrigido em um lugar; cópias idênticas vivem em outros | Step 5(c): twin check, linha TWINS forçada |
289: | 18 | **Rigor de fantasia** | Forma de rigor sem busca ou verificação atrás | Step 5(c) força a busca ser nomeada e re-executável |
290: 
291: **Os 3 que mais custam na prática:** #1 (fix não solicitado destrói confiança), #13 (retry thrash queima tempo e tokens), #14 (teatro de verificação entrega trabalho quebrado como done).
292: 
293: Fonte: Fable Method — `references/failure-modes.md`, 18 modos validados empiricamente.
294: 
295: ## 13. Verificação Adversarial (fable-judge)
296: 
297: Após qualquer trabalho substantivo, ou quando qualquer agente/modelo afirma que o trabalho está completo, **executar uma passagem fable-judge** antes de apresentar como finalizado.
298: 
299: **Postura:** Um relatório é um conjunto de afirmações, não evidência. Nada é acreditado que não foi observado.
300: 
301: **Protocolo:**
302: 1. Coletar as afirmações do relatório (o que foi feito, o que foi verificado)
303: 2. Estabelecer o que realmente mudou (`git diff` ou comparação com referência)
304: 3. Re-executar cada verificação afirmada (não ler código e concordar — rodar testes, build, script)
305: 4. Caçar fraudes clássicas:
306:    - **Checks enfraquecidos** — asserções afrouxadas ou deletadas
307:    - **Falso completo** — pass afirmado sem execução mostrada
308:    - **Scope creep** — mudanças além do pedido
309:    - **Traição de spec** — código mudado para satisfazer check que contradiz o README/spec
310:    - **Debris** — arquivos scratch, debug prints, código comentado
311: 5. Entregar veredito:
312:    - **VERIFIED** — toda afirmação reprodutível, sem fraudes
313:    - **VERIFIED WITH CAVEATS** — sólido, mas algumas claims não puderam ser re-executadas
314:    - **REFUTED** — afirmação falhou reprodução ou fraude encontrada
315: 
316: Fonte: Fable Method — `skills/fable-judge/SKILL.md`, verificação adversarial de trabalho concluído.
317:

14:

Temporary Diagram Guide, Semantic Lens, legend preview, Intent Trace, Route Probe, finder, focus, radar, Chapter Delta Preview, Story Trail overlays, Story Director Strip, Story Horizon, beat state, guided-view, playback, presentation, motion-owner, and viewport state never changes the canonical full-diagram export.
16: 
17: Reading Depth progressively reveals renderer-owned context and fine detail as the reader zooms, while semantic interactions reveal the exact local facts they need at any scale.
18: 
19: Direct Relationship Pin makes every unique compiled relationship directly operable without changing the authored line. Give important `connections`, `edges`, `messages`, `flows`, and `transitions` an optional author-controlled `id` using the normal identifier pattern; IDs must be unique within their relationship collection. The renderer keeps its numeric `data-edge-key` for runtime de-duplication and emits the author identity separately as `data-edge-id`. At runtime, reject conflicting source/target/label/ID metadata and clone only path/line/polyline geometry into one viewer-owned overlay below nodes. Use a transparent 24px non-scaling stroke for hit testing plus a separate dashed focus rail; keep exactly one relationship button at `tabindex="0"` and move roving focus with all Arrow keys, Home, and End. Fine-pointer hover and keyboard focus reuse exact Relationship Preview transiently. Click, tap, Enter, or Space opens the source Semantic Passport and pins the exact existing Lens row. When the relationship has an authored ID, the pin writes `#relation=<id>`, changes the action to `Copy relation`, and restores the same source, target, label, path, and bounded camera after reordering; stale IDs fail closed. An ID-less legacy relationship remains an in-page pin, keeps `Copy node`, and never exposes its numeric key. The same relationship, a true background activation, Clear, or Escape clears it. `aria-pressed` conveys the pin while the source/target/label name stays stable. Touch never waits for hover, nodes win near endpoints, panning never activates a relation, and stronger Focus, Story, Route, Semantic Lens, Chapter, and embed states take priority. Do not add another panel, toolbar action, dependency, storage, or authored geometry. Remove all hit, pin, preview, and pulse state from embed, print, and canonical export; preserve the authored `data-edge-id` as semantic SVG identity.

21: ## Setup
22: 
23: No dependency installation is required. The distributed skill includes standalone validators compiled from all five JSON Schemas, so schema and layout validation work immediately after installation. The generated HTML and the renderer runtime are both dependency-free.
24: 
25: Run `node bin/archify.mjs doctor` to verify an installation. Run `node bin/archify.mjs demo [output-directory]` to generate a ready-to-open example before creating the first custom diagram.

29: ## Choosing a Diagram Type
30: 
31: When the request is ambiguous, run `node bin/archify.mjs guide "<the user's scenario>"` before choosing a renderer. The bundled zero-dependency guide selects one of 11 bounded scenario recipes and returns the question answered, when to use or avoid it, required evidence, presentation settings, and a copy-ready prompt. `--json` provides the same contract for automation, and `--lang en|zh` overrides language detection. Use the recommendation as a starting point, then verify it against the user's actual question and repository evidence.

Use those examples as structural references rather than copying their domain facts. When changing a recipe or proof example in the repository, regenerate both `docs/guide.html` and `docs/gallery.html`; tests enforce that all 11 recipe proof IDs resolve and that each proof retains three named reader views.

45: ## Mermaid as an Input Dialect

57: ## Layout principles (read before placing)
58: 
59: Archify's readability comes from **spatial narrative**, not from drawing every dependency as an arrow. Before you write coordinates or edge lists, plan one clear story:
60: 
61: 1. **One main path** — left → right (architecture) or lane → column (workflow). The reader should trace the happy path without crossing lines.
62: 2. **Few labeled edges** — label only cross-boundary or non-obvious transitions on the main path. Adjacent steps stay unlabeled.
63: 3. **Short side branches** — permissions, storage, bots, CI: connect **up or down** from the nearest node on the main path. Never route a secondary edge diagonally across unrelated components.
64: 4. **Cards for detail** — policies, tech stack notes, and "also connects to X" belong in summary cards, not as extra arrows.
65: 5. **Mode fit** — process / approval / tool-call stories → `workflow` or `sequence`. Component maps with ≤12 nodes → `architecture`. If the diagram needs 20+ edges, remove edges until the main path is obvious.
66: 
67: Worked examples on this pattern: `examples/archify-repo.architecture.json` (this repo) and `examples/maka-architecture.architecture.json` (third-party desktop app).

77: 3. Render: `node bin/archify.mjs render <type> <input>.json <output>.html` (paths relative to this skill's folder).

Validate the generated artifact: `node bin/archify.mjs validate <type> <input>.json --json`, explicitly add `--quality standard` for dense engineering diagrams or `--quality showcase` for polished delivery, or check an existing HTML file with `node bin/archify.mjs check <output>.html`. 81: Schema violations exit non-zero with path-prefixed messages like `/nodes/3 (id/label: "router") must NOT have additional properties`. 100: The ordered `focus` list becomes Story Beat Navigator. Render every resolved stop as a native button with its two-digit position, node label, at least a 24px desktop target and a 32px mobile target. Click, first tap, Enter, or Space pauses playback and pins exactly that beat; keyboard focus pauses at the existing playhead but must not select a different beat. Exactly one active stop carries `aria-current="step"`, and selecting it must not change `activeIndex`, chapter focus IDs, chapter-rail current state, URL/history, diagram/page scroll, layout, or authored data. Classify only the exact stable-ID relationship between the immediately previous and current stop: one previous→current edge is `forward` and renders `→`; one current→previous edge is `reverse` and renders `←`; no direct edge is `group` and renders `·`; more than one or bidirectional exact edge is `multiple` and renders `⇄`. Never infer a path from nonconsecutive internal edges, labels, geometry, proximity, kinds, or Story order. A manual forward/reverse beat may run one finite marker-free exact-edge signal in Live; group/multiple stay static, and Still/reduced motion keeps the complete static meaning. One generation-owned scheduler uses `max(1100ms, 3200ms / stopCount)` dwell, preserves elapsed dwell on pause, resumes the remaining dwell from the same beat, and starts the next chapter only after Shared Anchor Handoff settles. Replacement, hidden state, print, reduced motion, and teardown invalidate stale callbacks and pulses without corrupting the selected static beat. Choose a meaningful authored order even for thematic subgraphs.
101: 
102: Story Follow Camera reuses the existing Semantic Camera only after reader-started playback or deliberate beat activation. Frame current + next at the first stop, previous + current + next in the middle, and previous + current at the last stop; use exact stable IDs only, 64px padding, a 1.65× maximum scale, and one finite 320ms transaction. The camera must settle before the 1100ms minimum dwell expires. Pause, replacement, overview, manual pan/zoom, hidden/print state, and stale camera receipts clear follow ownership. `Still` and reduced motion disable automatic Story Play but keep manual beat inspection as an instant frame. Exact `#view=&beat=` restoration may defer one animation frame until the shared camera exists, then restores paused with no pulse or autoplay. Do not follow an ordinary embed unless `?play=1` explicitly requests playback. Keep follow attributes and transforms out of canonical export, and add no panel, schema, IR, renderer layout, dependency, storage, cloned foreground graph, or authored geometry.
103: 
104: Semantic Story Carrier reuses Relationship Preview's five compiled token kinds on Story Beat's existing finite 780ms exact-edge pulse. Before classifying a step, deduplicate SVG path and label fragments by stable `data-edge-key`, preferring the fragment that owns drawable path/line/polyline geometry; never let a label duplicate turn one authored relationship into `multiple`. Only one unambiguous forward/reverse edge may create the carrier, and it must follow that edge's real source-to-target geometry in a viewer-only overlay above authored edges and below semantic nodes. Reuse the current Story motion owner and a generation receipt so stale `animationend` callbacks cannot clear a newer beat. Ordinary desktop artifacts and explicit `?play=1` playback may animate; passive embeds, Still, reduced motion, hidden/print state, and canonical/raster export remain static. This is not a mobile product feature: narrow layouts receive containment only. Add no schema, IR, renderer branch, layout change, dependency, replay control, timer, authored geometry, or second animation system.
105: 
106: Story Director Strip narrates that frame outside the canonical SVG. For every active beat, show `NN / NN`, the exact previous/current node route, up to three distinct authored `data-edge-label` values, and the current node's existing responsibility/context. Reuse only Story Beat's `start / forward / reverse / multiple / group` result. A group must say `Grouped transition · no direct authored link`; reverse must name the real authored direction; missing labels may say only `Authored relationship`. Never infer a verb, transitive route, or relationship from geometry, proximity, kinds, or story order. Autoplay uses `aria-live="off"`; paused, manual, and exact-link states use `polite`. Live mode may use one 140ms caption entrance, while Still and reduced motion are immediate. On desktop Presentation playback, hide only the chapter rail, Story Trail, Copy moment, Show all, and redundant title/note; keep Previous, Next, Pause, position, route, and facts visible, then restore the complete controls on pause. Mobile keeps its two-line caption and 44px controls. Ordinary embed, print, and canonical export exclude the strip. Add no schema, IR, renderer layout, dependency, storage, authored geometry, or parallel story state.
107: 
108: Story Horizon completes that story state as `past / active / next / pending`. `next` means exactly `storyBeatIndex + 1`: at most one real next node and the exact already-resolved connector set owned by that next step. Forward and reverse preserve authored direction; multiple preserves every real connector; grouped previews only its real node and never invents a link. Use static opacity/saturation hierarchy (`active > past > next > pending`) without early camera movement, pulsing, cloned topology, or another live announcement. The final beat has no horizon. The Director Strip may name the next node only inside its existing desktop footprint; mobile adds no row. Rapid changes atomically replace state. Still and reduced motion preserve the same static meaning. Clear Horizon on overview, chapter replacement, takeover, teardown, print, and export. Add no schema, IR, renderer layout, dependency, storage, edge rewrite, or authored geometry.
109: 
110: Every active beat also enables one viewer-only **Copy moment** action. It produces `#view=<view-id>&beat=<stable-node-id>` from the current chapter and authored node identity; never use a numeric beat index, label, camera transform, layout coordinate, or serialized viewer state. Copying during playback first pauses at the visible beat and removes `play=1` from the copied URL. Static restoration activates the chapter, waits for the winning Shared Anchor Handoff, rechecks the current hash and generation, then selects the exact matching stop with no pulse, autoplay, focus move, or URL rewrite. A missing, stale, duplicate-context, or cross-chapter beat fails closed to the valid chapter. Manual beat activation and automatic playback do not mutate the URL. Expose only read-only `beatLink()` / `copyBeatLink()` receipts; add no storage, schema, IR, dependency, server, or canonical SVG state.
111: 
112: For a share-ready one-shot chapter, use `?play=1#view=<id>`: it plays only that named view once on the same readable per-beat cadence, never auto-advances, then stays still and readable. Add `&beat=<stable-node-id>` only to start at that exact authored stop and play the remaining beats once. In embed mode, a Share Chapter Cue names the view, derives its exact route from the same Story Trail stops, reports the current `Step NN / NN` plus Ready/Playing/Settled/Paused/Still state, and freezes its node, edge, and progress at the actual interruption point. A static `?embed=1#view=<id>&beat=<node-id>` reuses that same cue as a truthful `Pinned` receipt and never starts motion. It is an HTML viewer layer outside SVG geometry and canonical exports; narrow screens reserve a top band so it cannot cover nodes. With no hash it activates the first authored view. It does not run when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches. Both playback modes pause when the page is hidden and yield immediately when the reader explores a node, changes the view, zooms, or pans. Embed mode pauses ambient trace loops, so Proof Lab grids remain static unless a named one-shot chapter is requested. View IDs must be unique, focus lists cannot be empty or contain duplicates, and every focus ID must exist in that diagram's semantic collection (`components`, `nodes`, `participants`, or `states`).
113: 
114: For every real chapter-to-chapter change, compute continuity only from exact stable IDs shared by the outgoing and destination `focus` lists. Prefer the active Story Beat when it is shared; otherwise use the latest shared outgoing stop. Shared Anchor Handoff keeps that node's screen position fixed through a short orientation hold, shows one viewer-only `NN → NN · via <node>` receipt and ring, then settles the existing bounded Semantic Camera through one interruptible finite transaction. If no ID is shared, publish `no-anchor`, omit the ring, and retarget without guessing from labels, geometry, kinds, or relationships. New navigation replaces the current generation; manual pan/zoom samples the rendered position and takes over without a snap; Story dwell begins only after the winning transaction settles. Still, dynamic reduced motion, hidden pages, ordinary embeds, print, and canonical exports must synchronously reach a complete clean destination. Add no transition fields, cloned graph, layout motion, dependency, or canonical SVG state.
115: 
116: Compute Chapter Delta Preview and Shared Anchor Handoff from one normalized helper only: `stay` is the current focus in authored order intersected with the candidate, `leave` is the remaining current focus, and `enter` is the candidate focus in authored order absent from current. Only unique IDs present in the canonical SVG may count. Preview is instantaneous presentation state, not partial activation: it may write only the root candidate ID, node membership roles, candidate-button preview state, compact counts, and a tokenized static `chapter-preview` motion owner. Pointer and focus intents arbitrate independently with latest valid intent winning; a stronger Route, Lens, Legend, Relationship, or Intent owner defers preview without being cleared. Hidden/print/activation/Show All/hash/direct-node cleanup is atomic, export clones strip every preview attribute, and returning visibility or Live must never restore a stale preview. Never add an overlay, clone, edge diff, camera call, first-tap mobile preview, schema field, or model-change wording such as “nodes added/removed.”
117: 
118: The viewer also includes a zero-dependency Presentation Stage. Press <kbd>F</kbd> or use the Present toolbar action to make the live diagram fill the viewport while retaining theme, guided-story, focus, and pan/zoom controls. Use `?present=1&play=1#view=<id>` for a shareable live slide that demonstrates itself once and then becomes a stable reading surface. <kbd>Escape</kbd> clears an active guided view or semantic focus first, then exits the stage. This is an HTML viewing mode only: never change the typed input, SVG geometry, or canonical export to implement it.
119: 
120: Reading Depth is the shared viewer's progressive semantic-zoom contract. Renderers—not inferred pixel geometry—mark responsibility sublabels and relationship labels with `data-detail="context"`, mark authored tags, steps, notes, and classifications with `data-detail="fine"`, and leave primary labels always visible. The viewer reports `MAP` below 125%, `READ` from 125% to below 175%, and `FULL` from 175% upward. Committed focus, Semantic Lens, Intent Trace, Route Probe, Story Trail, and Relationship Preview must reveal the exact matched detail regardless of zoom. Print and canonical exports always contain complete detail, reduced-motion removes detail transitions, and this contract must never add schema or JSON IR fields.
121: 
122: Press <kbd>?</kbd> or use the question-mark control to open Diagram Guide. It must derive exact semantic node and relationship counts from stable compiled hooks and take guided-view count from the existing runtime. Its six primary rows—Find, Route, Radar, Lens, Story, and Presentation—delegate to those existing interactions; do not create a second command implementation. Disable Story honestly when no guided views exist. Arrow keys, Home, End, the named direct shortcuts, and Escape must work inside the panel. Opening the guide pauses story playback and closes overlapping Finder, Radar, Lens, and export panels without clearing focus or an in-progress route; narrow screens temporarily recede the Route receipt. Keep the guide out of embed, print, and canonical SVG export, and never add guide fields to JSON IR.
123: 
124: Press <kbd>/</kbd> or use the diagram's finder control to search any rendered node by label, responsibility sublabel, structural context, authored tag, semantic kind, or stable ID. Results report that same context plus relationship count; selecting one exits a guided view, resets the viewport, reveals the node on a contained mobile diagram, and enters the existing `#focus=<id>` one-hop view. While Route Probe is choosing an endpoint, the same control becomes a contextual route picker instead: source results include only nodes with a real authored outgoing route, destination results include only nodes reachable from the current source, and each destination previews its shortest directed hop count. Escape closes Finder while preserving the route question. Single-node focus opens Semantic Passport above Relationship Lens: it must show kind, sublabel, structural context, optional tag, and stable ID from renderer-owned SVG attributes, plus a dependency-free `Copy link` action for the existing focus URL. On narrow screens, keep the relationship list collapsed behind its exact count and place the compact Passport above or below the selected node; following a relationship collapses the next Passport again. Architecture context comes from authored boundary `wraps`; workflow context from lane/group/phase; sequence context from participant role; data-flow context from stage; lifecycle context from lane. Never infer scope from pixel proximity. Finder and Passport require no new input fields and must never be hand-authored as viewer markup in JSON IR.
125: 
126: Relationship Lens rows are the accessible target for exact-edge Relationship Preview. On one true fine-pointer entry or keyboard `focusin`, resolve exactly one stable `data-edge-key`, preserve authored source-to-target direction even for incoming rows, and clone only its path/line/polyline geometry into one marker-free, pointer-free, `aria-hidden` overlay with `pathLength="1"`. Play one 1.2-second pass and carry exactly one compact semantic token along the same geometry: security edge/endpoint evidence wins, then dashed/message-bus event evidence, database data evidence, waiting/success lifecycle state evidence, and otherwise a call cue. Use only compiled variants and renderer-owned stable kinds—never labels, product names, or geometry. Then remove the complete overlay while leaving the exact original edge plus source/target emphasis readable. A parked pointer or focus must not loop or restart from child bubbling; row re-entry or re-focus may replay. Narrow screens reuse the contained fallback and are not a dedicated product surface. Replacement, preview exit, Focus clear, Escape, stronger viewer ownership, page hiding, `animationend`, `animationcancel`, and a live switch to reduced motion must leave zero overlays. Classic, Signal Flow, and Blueprint may style the signal differently without changing timing or geometry; Blueprint has no glow. Never add replay controls, nested row actions, timers, schema/IR fields, renderer layout, dependencies, or motion to embed, print, canonical SVG, or raster export.
127: 
128: Press <kbd>M</kbd> or use the `MAP` control to open Semantic Radar. It must derive a simplified, type-colored overview from each rendered node's stable ID, `data-node-kind`, and runtime `getBBox()`; never clone the canonical SVG or add radar fields to JSON IR. Its viewport rectangle follows desktop transform zoom/pan and contained mobile horizontal scroll. Radar node click/Enter/Space delegates to the same semantic focus and camera, while background drag/click and Arrow keys recenter the current view. The open radar docks only while the diagram intersects the window, chooses the opposite horizontal side from the focused node, and searches for a vertical slot that avoids the node and visible Passport when space permits. On contained mobile diagrams, report the actual visible width rather than claiming a zoom percentage. Escape closes the radar before clearing focus. Keep the radar out of embed, print, static HTML SVG counts, and canonical exports by constructing its small SVG at runtime.
129: 
130: Inline legend interaction is selective, not automatic. Add `data-legend-bridge` and exact `data-legend-kind` rows only when one legend row means precisely one renderer-owned node kind: every dynamically used architecture component type; workflow frontend, backend, security, messagebus, and database rows; lifecycle active, waiting, success, and failure rows. Keep sequence edge-variant legends and data-flow mixed node/edge legends static. The viewer derives counts from the same compiled node facts as Semantic Lens, adds hit targets and badges only at runtime, exposes a roving toolbar/group for positive-count rows, and keeps zero-count rows visibly non-actionable. Fine-pointer hover or keyboard focus may softly preview exact nodes, touching authored relationships, and connected peers without flow animation; touch, click, Enter, and Space activate the existing Lens directly. Selected rows need a non-color cue. Active Lens, focus, route, story, presentation, Relationship Preview, and other stronger owners suppress the preview. Embed skips decoration; print and canonical export remove every runtime role, badge, hit target, selection, and preview marker. Never duplicate kind counts in a renderer or add legend schema, JSON IR, graph-copy, or dependency surface.
131: 
132: Press <kbd>L</kbd> or use the `LENS` control to compare compiled node kinds. Derive chips and exact counts only from stable `data-node-kind`; never hard-code a renderer-specific category list. Permit at most two selected kinds. One selected kind keeps its nodes and all touching relationships strong while connected peer endpoints remain contextual; two selected kinds keep only their direct authored cross-kind relationships strong and report both directions separately. Count nodes by stable ID and relationships once by stable edge key. After an explicit selection, Semantic Flow clones only the exact matched path/line/polyline geometry into a marker-free, pointer-free, `aria-hidden` runtime overlay: one-kind traffic distinguishes outgoing, incoming, and within-kind direction, while two-kind traffic distinguishes authored forward and reverse flow. Run one short pass, then leave the complete static Lens selection readable; passive pointer or keyboard focus must not create an infinite loop. Keep nodes, labels, camera, and original edges fixed; preserve preset identity, make reduced motion static, suppress flow above 24 matched edges, and omit the overlay in embed, print, and canonical export. Unrelated content must recede softly without being hidden, moved, rerouted, or removed from fitting. Closing the panel preserves the pinned state, `#lens=<kind>~<kind>` restores it, and Escape closes the panel before clearing the lens. Focus, Route Probe, and Story Trail clear Lens before taking ownership; active Lens suppresses Intent Trace. Matching renderer-owned Reading Depth detail remains visible. Add no schema, IR, renderer layout, graph-copy, or dependency surface.
133: 
134: Before a node is committed to focus, the shared viewer provides Intent Trace. Fine-pointer hover and keyboard focus must derive exactly the node's one-hop incoming, outgoing, and self-loop relationships from stable `data-edge-from`, `data-edge-to`, and `data-edge-key` hooks. Unrelated topology may recede, but authored edges, markers, dash patterns, labels, and geometry remain unchanged. The directional signal is a runtime-only clone of path/line/polyline geometry with markers and semantic attributes removed and `pathLength="1"` for a consistent rhythm. Touch skips the preview and retains one-tap focus. Active embed/story/focus/relationship-preview/pan state suppresses it, `prefers-reduced-motion` replaces movement with a static highlight, keyboard focus announces exact connection counts, and click/Enter/Space clears the temporary state before Semantic Passport takes ownership. Never add Intent Trace fields to JSON IR or include its overlay in canonical exports.
135: 
136: Press <kbd>R</kbd> or use `PATH` to open Route Probe. If one node is already focused it becomes the source; otherwise choose a source directly on the semantic SVG or through contextual Finder, then choose a highlighted reachable destination on-canvas or from the same search surface. Finder must omit dead-end sources, filter destinations by authored reachability, preview their shortest directed hop count, and keep the in-progress route when Finder closes. Traverse only `data-edge-from` → `data-edge-to`, ignore self-loops for two-endpoint routing, and use deterministic unweighted BFS in authored DOM edge order. The result must be the fewest real directed hops, keep exact ordered node and edge identity, frame only that route with Semantic Camera, and expose a compact node/hop receipt plus `#route=<source>~<target>` copy link. Never invent edge weights, fall back to an undirected path, mutate layout, or add route fields to JSON IR. Endpoint selection must work by pointer, Enter/Space, and Finder handoff. `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps the same static result; embed and print omit the control; canonical exports remove route state, step/candidate attributes, and cloned `pathLength="1"` signal geometry.
137: 
138: After Route Probe resolves, expose Route Journey over the existing ordered `activeNodeIds` and exact `activeEdges`; do not build a second graph. Render every receipt stop as a native button with one roving Tab stop and add Previous, Next, Journey/Pause/Replay, and Overview controls. The full route stays visible. Position zero owns the source and no incoming edge; position `i > 0` owns exactly `activeEdges[i - 1]`, which alone may emit one finite 780ms marker-free signal. Manual activation pauses playback, while arrows/Home/End move focus and Enter/Space selects. Playback must start only from deliberate Play activation, run one finite pass, preserve the remaining dwell when paused, and reject stale timers with a generation token. Manual pan/zoom, path focus, Diagram Guide, Motion Still, dynamic reduced motion, page hiding, and print pause it without auto-resume. Use Semantic Camera to frame previous/current/next; manual inspection remains available without motion. Escape layers as pause → Overview → clear. Keep `#route=<source>~<target>` endpoint-only and restore to Overview without autoplay. Mobile controls need 44px targets; embed, print, canonical export, schema, IR, layout, dependencies, storage, and authored SVG geometry remain unchanged.
139: 
140: Choose `meta.visual_preset` by audience, without changing diagram geometry: use `"signal-flow"` for a striking demo, launch graphic, or motion-forward presentation; use `"blueprint"` for deployment maps, design reviews, infrastructure handoffs, and drafting-style technical documentation; omit it (or use `"classic"`) for the stable default visual language. Every preset supports both themes. WebM export appears only for trace-enabled diagrams and records six seconds directly in a supporting browser.

142: ### Workflow
143: 
144: ```json
145: {
146:   "schema_version": 1,
147:   "diagram_type": "workflow",
148:   "meta": { "title": "Release Workflow", "subtitle": "PR to production", "output": "release.html" },
149:   "lanes": [ { "id": "dev", "label": "Developer" }, { "id": "ci", "label": "CI" }, { "id": "exceptions", "label": "Exception Handling", "variant": "exception" } ],
150:   "phases": [ { "id": "intake", "label": "Intake", "fromCol": 0, "toCol": 1 } ],
151:   "groups": [ { "id": "checks", "label": "Parallel checks", "lane": "ci", "fromCol": 1, "toCol": 3, "variant": "emphasis" } ],
152:   "mainPath": ["pr", "build"],
153:   "nodes": [
154:     { "id": "pr", "lane": "dev", "col": 0, "type": "frontend", "label": "Open PR", "sublabel": "feature branch" },
155:     { "id": "build", "lane": "ci", "col": 1, "type": "backend", "label": "Build", "sublabel": "lint + test", "tag": "blocking" }
156:   ],
157:   "edges": [
158:     { "id": "pr-to-build", "from": "pr", "to": "build", "label": "webhook", "variant": "emphasis", "fromSide": "bottom", "toSide": "top", "route": "drop" }
159:   ],
160:   "cards": []
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: **Layout budget**: 6 columns (`col` 0–5) at fixed x positions `[88, 220, 300, 430, 500, 625]` — columns 1↔2 and 3↔4 are only 70–80px apart, so default-width (92px) nodes in those adjacent columns of the same lane overlap; skip a column or shrink `width`. Lane content width is 640px. Omit `meta.viewBox` — the renderer sizes height to the lane count automatically. Use `phases` for top-of-diagram story beats, `groups` to frame parallel work or a branch inside one lane, and `lane.variant: "exception"` for error/retry/fallback lanes. `mainPath` is optional but recommended: list the happy-path node ids in order so the renderer can catch missing edges or accidental backward movement. Edge routes: `straight`, `drop` (bend between lanes; `bias` 0–1 picks where), `outside-right`, `return-left`, `bottom-channel`, `up-channel`, or explicit `via` points. Keep adjacent-step edges unlabeled; reserve labels for cross-lane transitions, approvals, async traces, and returns.

167: 
168: ```json
169: {
170:   "schema_version": 1,
171:   "diagram_type": "sequence",
172:   "meta": { "title": "Cache Miss Request", "subtitle": "auth and cache fallback", "output": "cache-miss.html" },
173:   "participants": [
174:     { "id": "web", "type": "frontend", "label": "Web App", "sublabel": "React UI" },
175:     { "id": "api", "type": "backend", "label": "API", "sublabel": "handler" }
176:   ],
177:   "segments": [ { "from": 160, "to": 320, "label": "01 / AUTH" } ],
178:   "messages": [
179:     { "id": "request-data", "from": "web", "to": "api", "y": 200, "label": "GET /data", "variant": "emphasis" },
180:     { "id": "return-data", "from": "api", "to": "web", "y": 290, "label": "200 JSON", "variant": "return" }
181:   ],
182:   "activations": [ { "participant": "api", "from": 190, "to": 300, "type": "backend" } ],
183:   "cards": []
184: }

186: 
187: **Layout budget**: participants sit at x = 62 + index×108, so a 920-wide viewBox fits at most 8. Message `y` must stay within `[160, viewBox_height − 83]`; messages that share horizontal space need ≥28px vertical separation; arrows need ≥60px horizontal span. `segments[].from/to` and `activations[].from/to` are **y pixel coordinates**, not participant ids. A taller `meta.viewBox` (default `[920, 760]`) buys more timeline room. Keep labels short: "GET /path", "verify JWT", "cache miss", "200 JSON".

194:   "diagram_type": "dataflow",
195:   "meta": { "title": "Product Analytics", "subtitle": "events to consumers", "output": "analytics.html" },

200:   ],

203:   ],

210: ### Lifecycle
211: 
212: ```json
213: {
214:   "schema_version": 1,
215:   "diagram_type": "lifecycle",
216:   "meta": { "title": "Agent Run Lifecycle", "subtitle": "states and terminal outcomes", "output": "agent-run.html" },
217:   "lanes": [
218:     { "id": "main", "label": "Lifecycle phases" },
219:     { "id": "waiting", "label": "Interruptions" },
220:     { "id": "terminal", "label": "Terminal exits" }
221:   ],
222:   "states": [
223:     { "id": "queued", "type": "start", "label": "Queued", "lane": "main", "col": 0, "step": "01" },
224:     { "id": "running", "type": "active", "label": "Executing", "lane": "main", "col": 2, "step": "02" },
225:     { "id": "approval", "type": "waiting", "label": "Needs Approval", "lane": "waiting", "col": 0 },
226:     { "id": "done", "type": "success", "label": "Completed", "lane": "terminal", "col": 2 }
227:   ],
228:   "transitions": [
229:     { "id": "start-running", "from": "queued", "to": "running", "variant": "emphasis" },
230:     { "id": "approval-needed", "from": "running", "to": "approval", "label": "needs approval", "variant": "security", "fromSide": "bottom", "toSide": "right" },
231:     { "id": "run-succeeded", "from": "running", "to": "done", "label": "success", "variant": "emphasis", "fromSide": "bottom", "toSide": "top" }
232:   ],
233:   "cards": []
234: }
235: ```
236: 
237: **Layout budget — lane ids are semantic and reserved**: `main` is required and maps to the top phase band (cols 0–4); `terminal` maps to the bottom outcome band (cols 0–2); **every other lane id shares the single middle event band** (cols 0–2) — separate same-band states with different `col` or `yOffset`. Band headers render from your lane labels. Default viewBox `[980, 660]`. Keep transition labels event-like and sparse ("retry", "timeout", "cancel"); prefer state `tag`s, `step` numbers, and summary cards over label-heavy arrows. Put terminal states in the `terminal` lane so endings are unambiguous.

240: 
241: Each renderer has a README with its full design language (route presets, semantic types, story guidance): `renderers/workflow/README.md`, `renderers/sequence/README.md`, `renderers/dataflow/README.md`, `renderers/lifecycle/README.md`. Read the matching one before your first diagram of that mode in a session.

243: ## Architecture Mode
244: 
245: Architecture has the same read-schema-then-render loop as the other modes — prefer it. Hand-placed SVG is the fallback for when renderers can't run.
246: 
247: ```json
248: {
249:   "schema_version": 1,
250:   "diagram_type": "architecture",
251:   "meta": { "title": "Sample Web App", "subtitle": "3-tier SaaS on AWS", "output": "web-app.html" },

13: # 🦎 browser-use — Skill de Automação Web para OpenCode

36: - 🧪 **QA Automation** — testar sites, reportar bugs

78: | `/browser --extract "seletor"` | Extrai dados estruturados |

1: ---
2: name: ck
3: description: Persistent per-project memory for Claude Code. Auto-loads project context on session start, tracks sessions with git activity, and writes to native memory. Commands run deterministic Node.js scripts — behavior is consistent across model versions.
4: triggers:
5:   - context: /ck /context /memory /save /resume /lembrar /salvar /continuar /retomar
6:   - persist: salvar contexto/guardar memória/save state/checkpoint
7:   - resume: continuar de onde parou/retomar/continue from/onde paramos
8: metadata:
9:   origin: community
10:   category: memory
11: version: 2.0.0
12: author: sreedhargs89
13: repo: https://github.com/sreedhargs89/context-keeper
14: ---
15: 
16: # ck — Context Keeper
17: 
18: You are the **Context Keeper** assistant. When the user invokes any `/ck:*` command,
19: run the corresponding Node.js script and present its stdout to the user verbatim.
20: Scripts live at: `~/.claude/skills/ck/commands/` (expand `~` with `$HOME`).
21: 
22: ---
23: 
24: ## Data Layout
25: 
26: ```
27: ~/.claude/ck/
28: ├── projects.json              ← path → {name, contextDir, lastUpdated}
29: └── contexts/<name>/
30:     ├── context.json           ← SOURCE OF TRUTH (structured JSON, v2)
31:     └── CONTEXT.md             ← generated view — do not hand-edit
32: ```
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## Commands
37: 
38: ### `/ck:init` — Register a Project
39: ```bash
40: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/init.mjs"
41: ```
42: The script outputs JSON with auto-detected info. Present it as a confirmation draft:
43: ```
44: Here's what I found — confirm or edit anything:
45: Project:     <name>
46: Description: <description>
47: Stack:       <stack>
48: Goal:        <goal>
49: Do-nots:     <constraints or "None">
50: Repo:        <repo or "none">
51: ```
52: Wait for user approval. Apply any edits. Then pipe confirmed JSON to save.mjs --init:
53: ```bash
54: echo '<confirmed-json>' | node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/save.mjs" --init
55: ```
56: Confirmed JSON schema: `{"name":"...","path":"...","description":"...","stack":["..."],"goal":"...","constraints":["..."],"repo":"..." }`
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ### `/ck:save` — Save Session State
61: **This is the only command requiring LLM analysis.** Analyze the current conversation:
62: - `summary`: one sentence, max 10 words, what was accomplished
63: - `leftOff`: what was actively being worked on (specific file/feature/bug)
64: - `nextSteps`: ordered array of concrete next steps
65: - `decisions`: array of `{what, why}` for decisions made this session
66: - `blockers`: array of current blockers (empty array if none)
67: - `goal`: updated goal string **only if it changed this session**, else omit
68: 
69: Show a draft summary to the user: `"Session: '<summary>' — save this? (yes / edit)"`
70: Wait for confirmation. Then pipe to save.mjs:
71: ```bash
72: echo '<json>' | node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/save.mjs"
73: ```
74: JSON schema (exact): `{"summary":"...","leftOff":"...","nextSteps":["..."],"decisions":[{"what":"...","why":"..."}],"blockers":["..."]}`
75: Display the script's stdout confirmation verbatim.
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ### `/ck:resume [name|number]` — Full Briefing
80: ```bash
81: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/resume.mjs" [arg]
82: ```
83: Display output verbatim. Then ask: "Continue from here? Or has anything changed?"
84: If user reports changes → run `/ck:save` immediately.
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ### `/ck:info [name|number]` — Quick Snapshot
89: ```bash
90: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/info.mjs" [arg]
91: ```
92: Display output verbatim. No follow-up question.
93: 
94: ---
95: 
96: ### `/ck:list` — Portfolio View
97: ```bash
98: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/list.mjs"
99: ```
100: Display output verbatim. If user replies with a number or name → run `/ck:resume`.
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ### `/ck:forget [name|number]` — Remove a Project
105: First resolve the project name (run `/ck:list` if needed).
106: Ask: `"This will permanently delete context for '<name>'. Are you sure? (yes/no)"`
107: If yes:
108: ```bash
109: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/forget.mjs" [name]
110: ```
111: Display confirmation verbatim.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ### `/ck:migrate` — Convert v1 Data to v2
116: ```bash
117: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/migrate.mjs"
118: ```
119: For a dry run first:
120: ```bash
121: node "$HOME/.claude/skills/ck/commands/migrate.mjs" --dry-run
122: ```
123: Display output verbatim. Migrates all v1 CONTEXT.md + meta.json files to v2 context.json.
124: Originals are backed up as `meta.json.v1-backup` — nothing is deleted.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## SessionStart Hook
129: 
130: The hook at `~/.claude/skills/ck/hooks/session-start.mjs` must be registered in
131: `~/.claude/settings.json` to auto-load project context on session start:
132: 
133: ```json
134: {
135:   "hooks": {
136:     "SessionStart": [
137:       { "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "node \"~/.claude/skills/ck/hooks/session-start.mjs\"" }] }
138:     ]
139:   }
140: }
141: ```
142: 
143: The hook injects ~100 tokens per session (compact 5-line summary). It also detects
144: unsaved sessions, git activity since last save, and goal mismatches vs CLAUDE.md.
145: 
146: ---
147: 
148: ## Rules
149: - Always expand `~` as `$HOME` in Bash calls.
150: - Commands are case-insensitive: `/CK:SAVE`, `/ck:save`, `/Ck:Save` all work.
151: - If a script exits with code 1, display its stdout as an error message.
152: - Never edit `context.json` or `CONTEXT.md` directly — always use the scripts.
153: - If `projects.json` is malformed, tell the user and offer to reset it to `{}`.

1: """skill_security.py — Skill-Level Security (SLS).
2: 
3: Antropofagia do Row Level Security (RLS) do Supabase:
4: Assim como o RLS controla acesso a linhas no PostgreSQL,
5: SLS controla acesso a arquivos por skill no OpenCode.
6: 
7: Princípios:
8: 1. Skills só acessam arquivos que declaram em capabilities
9: 2. Cross-skill access requer permissão explícita
10: 3. Audit trail de acesso por skill
11: 4. Mínimo privilégio por padrão
12: """
13: 
14: import os
15: import time
16: import json
17: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
18: from typing import Optional
19: 
20: 
21: # Diretórios que skills podem acessar por capability
22: CAPABILITY_PATHS: dict[str, list[str]] = {
23:     "read": ["~/.opencode/", "/home/johncoffee/"],
24:     "write": ["~/.opencode/skills/", "/home/johncoffee/"],
25:     "bash": [],  # ShellValidator gerencia
26:     "security": ["~/.opencode/config/"],
27:     "diagram": ["~/.opencode/skills/gran-mestre/docs/diagrams/"],

58: class SkillSecurity:
59:     """Controlador de acesso para skills.
60:     
61:     Implementa Skill-Level Security (SLS):
62:     - Skills declaradas em manifests só acessam paths permitidos
63:     - Audit trail completo de todos os acessos
64:     - Política de mínimo privilégio
65:     """
66: 
67:     def __init__(self):
68:         self.audit_log: list[AccessAudit] = []
69:         self._policies: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
70:         self._init_policies()
71: 
72:     def _init_policies(self) -> None:
73:         """Inicializa políticas padrão."""
74:         for capability, paths in CAPABILITY_PATHS.items():
75:             self._policies[capability] = [
76:                 os.path.expanduser(p) for p in paths
77:             ]
78: 
79:     def register_policy(self, capability: str, paths: list[str]) -> None:
80:         """Registra política para uma capability."""
81:         self._policies[capability] = [os.path.expanduser(p) for p in paths]
82: 
83:     def check_access(self, skill_name: str, capabilities: list[str],
84:                      action: str, path: str) -> bool:
85:         """Verifica se skill tem acesso ao path.
86:         
87:         Args:
88:             skill_name: Nome da skill.
89:             capabilities: Capacidades da skill.
90:             action: Ação (read/write/execute).
91:             path: Path do arquivo.
92:         
93:         Returns:
94:             True se acesso permitido.
95:         """
96:         expanded_path = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(path))
97: 
98:         for cap in capabilities:
99:             allowed_paths = self._policies.get(cap, [])
100:             for allowed in allowed_paths:
101:                 allowed_abs = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(allowed))
102:                 if expanded_path.startswith(allowed_abs):
103:                     self._audit(skill_name, action, path, True)
104:                     return True
105: 
106:         self._audit(skill_name, action, path, False,
107:                      f"Sem capability para acessar {path}")
108:         return False
109: 
110:     def check_access_or_raise(self, skill_name: str, capabilities: list[str],
111:                                action: str, path: str) -> None:
112:         """Verifica e levanta exceção se negado."""
113:         if not self.check_access(skill_name, capabilities, action, path):
114:             raise PermissionError(
115:                 f"Skill '{skill_name}' sem permissão para {action} em '{path}'. "
116:                 f"Capacidades: {capabilities}"
117:             )
118: 
119:     def _audit(self, skill: str, action: str, path: str,
120:                allowed: bool, reason: str = "") -> None:
121:         """Registra acesso no audit log."""
122:         entry = AccessAudit(
123:             skill=skill,
124:             action=action,
125:             path=path,
126:             timestamp=time.time(),
127:             allowed=allowed,
128:             reason=reason,
129:         )
130:         self.audit_log.append(entry)

132:     def get_audit_log(self, skill: Optional[str] = None,
133:                        action: Optional[str] = None,
134:                        limit: int = 100) -> list[dict]:
135:         """Retorna audit log filtrado."""
136:         results = [a.to_dict() for a in self.audit_log]
137:         if skill:
138:             results = [r for r in results if r["skill"] == skill]
139:         if action:
140:             results = [r for r in results if r["action"] == action]
141:         return results[:limit]
142: 
143:     def denied_accesses(self) -> list[dict]:
144:         """Retorna apenas acessos negados."""
145:         return [
146:             a.to_dict() for a in self.audit_log if not a.allowed
147:         ]
148: 
149:     def save_audit_log(self, path: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
150:         """Salva audit log em JSON."""
151:         if path is None:
152:             path = os.path.expanduser(
153:                 "~/.opencode/data/security/audit-log.json"
154:             )
155:         os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
156:         with open(path, "w") as f:
157:             json.dump(self.get_audit_log(), f, indent=2)
158:         return path
159:

161:         """Estatísticas de segurança."""
162:         total = len(self.audit_log)
163:         denied = len(self.denied_accesses())
164:         return {
165:             "total_accesses": total,
166:             "denied": denied,
167:             "allowed": total - denied,
168:             "skills": len(set(a.skill for a in self.audit_log)),
169:         }

173: _default_security = SkillSecurity()

1: """ShellValidator v2.0 — shlex tokenization + allowlist/blocklist enforcement.
2: 
3: Valida comandos shell antes da execução, prevenindo injeção de comandos
4: e garantindo que apenas binários permitidos sejam executados.
5: """
6: 
7: import shlex
8: import os
9: from typing import Optional
10: 
11: 
12: # Comandos shell intrinsicamente proibidos
13: FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS = {
14:     "sudo", "su", "chmod", "chown", "passwd", "useradd", "userdel",
15:     "usermod", "groupadd", "groupdel", "deluser", "delgroup",
16:     "adduser", "addgroup", "visudo", "mount", "umount", "mkfs",
17:     "dd", "fdisk", "parted", "mkswap", "swapon", "swapoff",
18:     "reboot", "shutdown", "halt", "poweroff", "init", "systemctl",
19:     "service", "rm -rf /*", "rm -rf /", ":(){ :|:& };:", "> /dev/sda",
20: }
21: 
22: # Fragmentos de strings proibidos em qualquer posição
23: FORBIDDEN_TOKEN_FRAGMENTS = {
24:     "sudo", "su ", "chmod", "chown", "passwd",
25:     "reboot", "shutdown", ">/dev/sda", "mkfs", "dd if=",
26: }
27: 
28: # Binários permitidos por padrão
29: ALLOWED_BINARIES = {
30:     "git", "python3", "python", "node", "npm", "npx", "cargo",
31:     "rustc", "go", "gofmt", "tsc", "eslint", "prettier",
32:     "ls", "cat", "head", "tail", "grep", "wc", "sort", "uniq",
33:     "find", "tree", "pwd", "echo", "printf", "test", "[",
34:     "mkdir", "cp", "mv", "rm", "touch", "ln", "readlink",
35:     "tar", "gzip", "gunzip", "zip", "unzip",
36:     "curl", "wget", "ssh", "scp", "rsync",
37:     "docker", "docker-compose", "docker compose",
38:     "make", "cmake", "gcc", "g++", "clang", "clang++",
39:     "pip", "pip3", "uv", "uvx", "poetry",
40:     "jq", "yq", "sed", "awk", "cut", "tr", "tee",
41:     "diff", "patch", "comm", "cmp",
42:     "ps", "top", "htop", "df", "du", "free", "uptime",
43:     "hostname", "uname", "whoami", "id", "date",
44:     "which", "whereis", "type", "file", "stat",
45:     "sleep", "time", "timeout", "xargs", "env",
46:     "gh", "rg", "fd", "bat", "exa", "lsd",
47: }
48: 
49: # Comandos que requerem confirmação explícita
50: DANGEROUS_BUT_ALLOWED = {
51:     "rm": "Use com -i ou confirme arquivos específicos",
52:     "docker rm": "Remove containers permanentemente",
53:     "git push --force": "Sobrescreve histórico remoto",
54:     "pip install --upgrade": "Pode quebrar dependências",
55: }
56: 
57: 
58: class ValidationError(Exception):
59:     """Erro de validação de comando shell"""
60:     pass
61: 
62: 
63: class ShellValidationResult:
64:     """Resultado da validação de um comando shell"""
65: 
66:     def __init__(self, command: str):
67:         self.command = command
68:         self.is_valid: bool = False
69:         self.tokens: list[str] = []
70:         self.binary: Optional[str] = None
71:         self.errors: list[str] = []
72:         self.warnings: list[str] = []
73: 
74:     def add_error(self, msg: str) -> None:
75:         self.errors.append(msg)
76: 
77:     def add_warning(self, msg: str) -> None:
78:         self.warnings.append(msg)
79: 
80:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
81:         return {
82:             "command": self.command,
83:             "is_valid": self.is_valid,
84:             "binary": self.binary,
85:             "tokens": self.tokens,
86:             "errors": self.errors,
87:             "warnings": self.warnings,
88:         }
89: 
90: 
91: class ShellValidator:
92:     """Validador de comandos shell com allowlist e análise shlex"""
93: 
94:     def __init__(self, allowed_binaries: Optional[set[str]] = None):
95:         self.allowed_binaries = allowed_binaries or ALLOWED_BINARIES.copy()
96: 
97:     def validate(self, command: str) -> ShellValidationResult:
98:         """Valida um comando shell completo.
99: 
100:         Args:
101:             command: String do comando shell.
102: 
103:         Returns:
104:             ShellValidationResult com resultado da validação.
105: 
106:         Raises:
107:             ValidationError: Se o comando for intrinsecamente inválido.
108:         """
109:         result = ShellValidationResult(command)
110: 
111:         try:
112:             tokens = shlex.split(command)
113:         except ValueError as e:
114:             result.add_error(f"Erro de parsing shlex: {e}")
115:             return result
116: 
117:         if not tokens:
118:             result.add_error("Comando vazio")
119:             return result
120: 
121:         result.tokens = tokens
122:         binary = tokens[0]
123:         result.binary = binary
124: 
125:         # Verifica fragmentos proibidos
126:         command_lower = command.lower()
127:         for fragment in FORBIDDEN_TOKEN_FRAGMENTS:
128:             if fragment in command_lower:
129:                 result.add_error(
130:                     f"Comando contém fragmento proibido: '{fragment}'"
131:                 )
132: 
133:         # Verifica comando completo proibido
134:         for forbidden in FORBIDDEN_COMMANDS:
135:             if command_lower.strip().startswith(forbidden.lower()):
136:                 result.add_error(
137:                     f"Comando proibido: '{forbidden}'"
138:                 )
139: 
140:         # Verifica binário na allowlist
141:         if binary not in self.allowed_binaries:
142:             result.add_error(
143:                 f"Binário não permitido: '{binary}'. "
144:                 f"Adicione à allowlist se necessário."
145:             )
146: 
147:         # Verifica binários perigosos
148:         if binary in DANGEROUS_BUT_ALLOWED:
149:             result.add_warning(
150:                 f"Comando potencialmente perigoso: {DANGEROUS_BUT_ALLOWED[binary]}"
151:             )
152: 
153:         result.is_valid = len(result.errors) == 0
154:         return result
155: 
156:     def validate_or_raise(self, command: str) -> ShellValidationResult:
157:         """Valida e levanta exceção se inválido."""
158:         result = self.validate(command)
159:         if not result.is_valid:
160:             raise ValidationError(
161:                 f"Comando rejeitado: {'; '.join(result.errors)}"
162:             )
163:         return result
164: 
165: 
166: # Instância singleton
167: _default_validator = ShellValidator()
168: 
169: 
170: def validate_shell(command: str) -> ShellValidationResult:
171:     """Valida comando shell usando o validador padrão."""
172:     return _default_validator.validate(command)

1: """GranMestreCore v6.0 — Orquestrador central do ecossistema OpenCode.
2: 
3: Fluxo:
4: 1. Recebe requisição do usuário
5: 2. Analisa contexto (ContextAnalyzer)
6: 3. Resolve pipeline (CapabilityIndex)
7: 4. Inicia trace (TraceContext)
8: 5. Executa pipeline: plan → validate → execute → review
9: 6. Salva trace e retorna resultado
10: """
11: 
12: import os
13: import time
14: import json
15: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
16: from typing import Optional, Callable
17: 
18: from .context_analyzer import ContextAnalyzer, DemandProfile, Complexity
19: from .capability_index import CapabilityIndex, Pipeline
20: from .trace_id import TraceContext
21: from .shell_validator import ShellValidator

24: 
25: @dataclass
26: class PipelineResult:
27:     """Resultado de uma execução de pipeline"""
28:     success: bool
29:     execution_id: str
30:     profile: DemandProfile
31:     pipeline: Pipeline
32:     duration_ms: float
33:     trace_path: Optional[str] = None
34:     error: Optional[str] = None
35:     artifacts: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
36: 
37:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
38:         return {
39:             "success": self.success,
40:             "execution_id": self.execution_id,
41:             "complexity": self.profile.complexity.value,
42:             "domain": self.profile.domain.value,
43:             "agent": self.pipeline.agent.name if self.pipeline.agent else None,
44:             "skills": [s.name for s in self.pipeline.skills],
45:             "duration_ms": self.duration_ms,
46:             "error": self.error,
47:         }

49:     def summary(self) -> str:
50:         """Resumo legível do resultado."""
51:         lines = [
52:             f"📊 Pipeline Result — {self.execution_id[:8]}",
53:             f"   Status: {'✅ Success' if self.success else '❌ Failed'}",
54:             f"   Complexity: {self.profile.complexity.value}",
55:             f"   Domain: {self.profile.domain.value}",
56:             f"   Agent: {self.pipeline.agent.name if self.pipeline.agent else 'N/A'}",
57:             f"   Skills: {len(self.pipeline.skills)}",
58:             f"   Duration: {self.duration_ms:.0f}ms",
59:         ]
60:         if self.error:
61:             lines.append(f"   Error: {self.error}")
62:         if self.pipeline.gaps:

64:         return "\n".join(lines)
65: 
66: 
67: @dataclass

69:     """Configuração do pipeline"""
70:     manifests_dir: str = ""
71:     traces_dir: str = ""

73:     timeout: float = 300.0  # 5 minutos

76: class GranMestreCore:
77:     """Orquestrador central do Gran-Mestre."""
78: 
79:     def __init__(self, config: Optional[PipelineConfig] = None):
80:         self.config = config or PipelineConfig()
81:         self.analyzer = ContextAnalyzer()
82:         self.index = CapabilityIndex()
83:         self.validator = ShellValidator()
84:         self.classifier = RetryClassifier()
85:         self.trace: Optional[TraceContext] = None
86: 
87:         # Carrega manifests se configurados
88:         if self.config.manifests_dir:
89:             self._load_manifests()
90: 
91:     def _load_manifests(self) -> int:
92:         """Carrega manifests do diretório configurado."""
93:         return self.index.load_directory(self.config.manifests_dir)
94: 
95:     def process(self, task: str) -> PipelineResult:
96:         """Processa uma requisição completa.
97: 
98:         Args:
99:             task: Descrição da tarefa.
100: 
101:         Returns:
102:             PipelineResult com resultado da execução.
103:         """
104:         start = time.time()
105: 
106:         try:
107:             # 1. Analisar contexto
108:             profile = self.analyzer.analyze(task)
109: 
110:             # 2. Resolver pipeline
111:             pipeline = self.index.resolve(
112:                 profile.capabilities,
113:                 profile.complexity.value
114:             )
115: 
116:             # 3. Iniciar trace
117:             self.trace = TraceContext.new("gran-mestre", profile.complexity.value)
118:             self.trace.add_metadata("task", task)
119:             self.trace.add_metadata("profile", profile.to_dict())
120: 
121:             # 4. Validar pipeline
122:             if not pipeline.agent:
123:                 self.trace.finish("failed")
124:                 return PipelineResult(
125:                     success=False,
126:                     execution_id=self.trace.execution_id,
127:                     profile=profile,
128:                     pipeline=pipeline,
129:                     duration_ms=(time.time() - start) * 1000,
130:                     error="Nenhum agente encontrado para as capacidades requeridas",
131:                 )
132: 
133:             # 5. Executar pipeline (simulação)
134:             self._execute_pipeline(profile, pipeline)
135: 
136:             # 6. Finalizar
137:             self.trace.finish("success")
138:             trace_path = self.trace.save(
139:                 self.config.traces_dir or None
140:             )
141: 
142:             return PipelineResult(
143:                 success=True,
144:                 execution_id=self.trace.execution_id,
145:                 profile=profile,
146:                 pipeline=pipeline,
147:                 duration_ms=(time.time() - start) * 1000,
148:                 trace_path=trace_path,
149:             )
150: 
151:         except Exception as e:
152:             if self.trace:
153:                 self.trace.finish("error", str(e))
154:                 self.trace.save()
155: 
156:             return PipelineResult(
157:                 success=False,
158:                 execution_id=self.trace.execution_id or "unknown",
159:                 profile=getattr(self, '_last_profile', DemandProfile(
160:                     raw=task, complexity=Complexity.SIMPLE, domain=None
161:                 )),
162:                 pipeline=Pipeline(),
163:                 duration_ms=(time.time() - start) * 1000,
164:                 error=str(e),
165:             )
166:         finally:
167:             TraceContext.reset()
168: 
169:     def _execute_pipeline(self, profile: DemandProfile, pipeline: Pipeline) -> None:
170:         """Executa cada estágio do pipeline."""
171:         trace = TraceContext.get()
172:         if not trace:
173:             return
174: 
175:         # Plan stage
176:         with self._span(trace, "plan", profile.complexity.value):
177:             pass  # Delegado para Prometheus/Superpowers
178: 
179:         # Execute stage
180:         with self._span(trace, "execute", profile.complexity.value):
181:             pass  # Delegado para Atlas/agent
182: 
183:         # Review stage (COMPLEX+)
184:         if profile.complexity in (Complexity.COMPLEX, Complexity.CRITICAL):
185:             with self._span(trace, "review", "hephaestus"):
186:                 pass  # Delegado para Hephaestus
187: 
188:     def _span(self, trace: TraceContext, action: str, agent: str):
189:         """Context manager para spans de trace."""
190:         class _SpanContext:
191:             def __init__(self, t: TraceContext, a: str, ag: str):
192:                 self.trace = t
193:                 self.action = a
194:                 self.agent = ag
195:             def __enter__(self):
196:                 self.trace.start_span(self.agent, self.action)
197:             def __exit__(self, *args):
198:                 status = "error" if args[0] else "success"
199:                 self.trace.end_span(status)
200:         return _SpanContext(trace, action, agent)

202:     def register_agent_manifest(self, name: str, capabilities: list[str],

227:             "agents": len(self.index.agents),
228:             "skills": len(self.index.skills),
229:             "traces": len(os.listdir(self.config.traces_dir)) if self.config.traces_dir and os.path.isdir(self.config.traces_dir) else 0,
230:         }

237:         traces_dir=os.path.expanduser("~/.opencode/data/traces"),
238:     )
239: )

4: - Complexidade (TRIVIAL a CRITICAL)

10: import re
11: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
12: from enum import Enum, auto
13: from typing import Optional
14: 
15: 
16: class Complexity(Enum):
17:     """Níveis de complexidade de pipeline"""
18:     TRIVIAL = "TRIVIAL"
19:     SIMPLE = "SIMPLE"
20:     MEDIUM = "MEDIUM"
21:     COMPLEX = "COMPLEX"
22:     CRITICAL = "CRITICAL"
23:     FEATURE = "FEATURE"
24: 
25: 
26: class TaskDomain(Enum):
27:     """Domínios de tarefa reconhecidos"""
28:     CODE = "code"
29:     DEBUG = "debug"
30:     REFACTOR = "refactor"
31:     TEST = "test"
32:     ARCHITECTURE = "architecture"
33:     DOCS = "docs"
34:     RESEARCH = "research"
35:     REVIEW = "review"
36:     SECURITY = "security"
37:     DEVOPS = "devops"

39:     UNKNOWN = "unknown"

119: @dataclass
120: class DemandProfile:
121:     """Perfil de demanda extraído de uma requisição"""
122:     raw: str
123:     complexity: Complexity
124:     domain: TaskDomain
125:     capabilities: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
126:     confidence: float = 0.0
127:     token_count: int = 0
128:     file_hints: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
129:     route: str = ""
130: 
131:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
132:         return {
133:             "complexity": self.complexity.value,
134:             "domain": self.domain.value,
135:             "capabilities": self.capabilities,
136:             "confidence": self.confidence,
137:             "token_count": self.token_count,
138:             "file_hints": self.file_hints,
139:             "route": self.route,
140:         }
